drawdown_context: Athletic-apparel issuer trading at $6.54 on 2025-05-15 vs ~$11 a year earlier (-41% drawdown). The FY24 10-K (filed 2024-05-29) closed a year of multiple shocks: (1) founder Kevin Plank returned as CEO in April 2024 displacing Stephanie Linnartz after barely 15 months — the third CEO transition in three years (Frisk to Linnartz March 2023, Linnartz to Plank April 2024); (2) Board approved a Fiscal 2025 Restructuring Plan on May 15, 2024 for $70-90M of pre-tax charges; (3) management identified MATERIAL WEAKNESSES in ICFR as of March 31, 2024 (period-end financial reporting process / balance sheet reconciliations / GL classification), forcing PRIOR-PERIOD FINANCIAL STATEMENT REVISIONS to correct overstated revenues, understated COGS, and understated SG&A; (4) ongoing securities class action regarding 'pull forward' sales with trial scheduled July 15, 2024. The three pre-cutoff 10-Qs (Q1 Aug 2024, Q2 Nov 2024, Q3 Feb 2025) show: $434M class-action settlement reached June 20, 2024 (≈50% of $859M cash); restructuring expanded to $140-160M Sept 5, 2024 (~2x original); 9M FY25 revenue $3.98B vs $4.37B prior year (-8.8%); 9M FY25 net loss $(133.8)M vs +$225.5M prior year — yet management RE-AUTHORIZED a fresh $500M buyback May 15, 2024 (same day as restructuring announce) and executed an ASR at $8.76 in December 2024 while material weaknesses remained UNREMEDIATED.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Based on that evaluation, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer have concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures were not effective as of March 31, 2024, due to the material weaknesses in our internal control over financial reporting described below.' Material weaknesses: (i) 'failure to design and maintain effective controls over certain aspects of the period-end financial reporting process, including the review and execution of certain balance sheet account reconciliations,' and (ii) 'we did not design and maintain effective controls over the classification and presentation of general ledger accounts in the appropriate financial statement line items within the consolidated financial statements.' Triggered REVISION of previously issued annual consolidated financial statements correcting: (1) overstated net revenues from promotional gift card / e-commerce errors, (2) understated COGS from duty cost errors, (3) understated SG&A.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm material weakness disclosure + revision (existence check). Mode B: track REMEDIATION across all 3 pre-cutoff 10-Qs. If management is honest, remediation should progress visibly over 9 months. Compare ICFR remediation language in 10-K (May 2024) vs Q3 FY25 10-Q (Feb 2025).
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q3 FY25 10-Q (filed Feb 6, 2025 — 8 months after material weakness identified): 'While we have taken steps to implement our remediation plan, these material weaknesses will not be considered fully remediated until we complete the design and implementation of the applicable controls, and they operate for a sufficient period of time and management has concluded through testing that the controls are operating effectively.' And: 'No change in our internal control over financial reporting ... occurred during the quarter ended December 31, 2024 that has materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.' Translation: AS OF FEB 6 2025, MATERIAL WEAKNESSES REMAIN UNREMEDIATED — 9+ months after first disclosure. Prior-period revisions touched the most consequential income-statement line items (revenue, COGS, SG&A). Auditor PwC's Critical Audit Matter is REVENUE RECOGNITION specifically, signaling auditor focus on the same area where the company had to correct prior reporting.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: A material weakness in period-end financial reporting that REQUIRED PRIOR-PERIOD REVISION to revenue/COGS/SG&A is the most serious form of ICFR finding short of a restatement, and at a company already defending a securities class action that alleges sales-period shifting ('pull forward'), it lands directly in the highest-discrimination forensic bucket. Nine months of remediation runway with NO ICFR improvement disclosed at Q3 FY25 is honest reporting (good Mode A) but signals that the controls weakness is structural, not transactional. The auditor's choice of revenue recognition as its sole Critical Audit Matter is independent confirmation that the area of weakness is the area of greatest auditor concern.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K (May 2024): 'Fiscal 2025 Restructuring Plan On May 15, 2024, the Company's Board of Directors approved a restructuring plan ... the Company expects to incur total estimated pre-tax restructuring and related charges of approximately $70 million to $90 million, during Fiscal 2025.' Q1 FY25 10-Q (Aug 8 2024) restates same $70-90M range. Q3 FY25 10-Q (Feb 6 2025): 'On September 5, 2024, our Board of Directors approved a $70 million increase to the 2025 restructuring plan, resulting in an updated restructuring plan of approximately $140 million to $160 million ... to be incurred during Fiscal 2025 and the fiscal year ending March 31, 2026.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: restructuring-plan magnitude evolution and time-horizon extension. A restructuring plan that DOUBLES in size and stretches into the next fiscal year less than 4 months after announcement is a quantitative tell of underlying business deterioration vs management's initial diagnosis. Compare initial 10-K vs Q3 10-Q.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Original 10-K (May 15, 2024): $70-90M / Fiscal 2025 only. Sept 5, 2024 (110 days later, between Q1 and Q2 10-Qs): +$70M increase to $140-160M and EXTENDED to also cover Fiscal 2026. Charges actually incurred 9M FY25: $57.4M (Q1 $33.7M + Q2 ~$5.9M + Q3 $17.8M). Remaining: $102.6M. Composition shifted: cash charges went $50M→$75M (+50%), non-cash went $40M→$85M (+113%). Non-cash $78M in 'facility, software, and other asset-related charges and impairments' = asset write-downs masquerading as restructuring.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Doubling a restructuring plan within 110 days of its announcement is a meaningful negative tell — either (a) the initial diagnosis was wrong, (b) the business deteriorated faster than management expected, or (c) management seized the cover of an already-announced restructuring to absorb additional asset impairments. The non-cash component disproportionately grew (+113% vs cash +50%), consistent with interpretation (c). A May-2024 10-K reader cannot anticipate the Sept-2024 expansion, but a Q3 FY25 reader sees the trajectory: this is a restructuring plan in escalation, not in execution. Combined with the founder-returns-as-CEO context, this looks like Plank using the first 12 months to right-size by writing down assets — classic new-CEO 'big bath' pattern.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K (May 2024) Note 10: 'On March 23, 2017, three separate securities cases ... were consolidated under the caption In re Under Armour Securities Litigation, Case No. 17-cv-00388-RDB ... The TAC alleges that the defendants supposedly concealed purportedly declining consumer demand for certain of the Company's products between the third quarter of 2015 and the fourth quarter of 2016 by ... engaging in undisclosed and allegedly improper sales and accounting practices, including shifting sales between quarterly periods allegedly to appear healthier ... The District Court has scheduled trial to begin on July 15, 2024. The Company continues to believe that the claims asserted in the Consolidated Securities Action are without merit and intends to defend this matter vigorously.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm litigation exists. Mode B: track CLAIM EVOLUTION from 10-K (will defend vigorously, trial July 15) to pre-cutoff 10-Qs. A securities class action that goes to trial after class certification + summary judgment denial is a binary risk; settlement post-filing is the dominant signal.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 FY25 10-Q (filed Aug 8, 2024): 'On June 20, 2024, the defendants reached an agreement with the plaintiffs to enter into a settlement resolving the Consolidated Securities Action. Under the terms of the Settlement, the Company will pay or will cause to be paid an amount equal to $434 million to the members of the class.' Plus two non-monetary provisions: (1) separate Chair/CEO roles for at least three years from court approval, (2) all RSUs/RSAs to CEO/CFO/CLO during the Three-Year Period must have performance-based vesting. Stipulation of settlement July 12 2024; preliminary approval July 22 2024; final approval hearing November 7 2024. $434M = 50.5% of $858.7M FY24 cash, ~3.7x FY24 operating cash flow ($354M), and 75% of FY24 pre-tax income.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K (May 29 2024) used 'without merit' / 'defend vigorously' language while privately, 22 days later (June 20 2024), the company was already reaching agreement to pay $434M plus governance concessions that imply admission of the originally-alleged Chair/CEO concentration concern. This is the textbook divergence between disclosed litigation posture and actual settlement readiness. A Mode-A only investigator stops at 'will defend vigorously'; a Mode-B investigator tracks the post-filing 10-Q and finds a settlement that consumes half the cash balance. The required NON-monetary provisions (separate Chair/CEO + performance-only RSU vesting for the top three executives) are de facto governance reforms imposed on Plank — implicitly acknowledging that the corporate-governance allegations had merit even if the company doesn't formally admit it.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K: 'On May 15, 2024, subsequent to the fiscal year end, our Board of Directors authorized the repurchase of up to $500 million (exclusive of fees and commissions) of outstanding shares of our Class C Common Stock through May 31, 2027.' Q3 FY25 10-Q (filed Feb 6 2025) Issuer-Purchases table: October 2024 zero / November 2024 zero / December 2024 2,781,424 Class C shares at $8.76 average via accelerated share repurchase = $24.4M. Note that the Chief Legal Officer Mehri Shadman Form 4 (filed Nov 19 2024) shows sales: 11/15/2024 sold 17,240 Class C at $8.7601 and 11/18/2024 sold 9,639 Class C at $8.8081.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: insider-sell-vs-buyback timing asymmetry (insider_vs_calendar). The May-15-2024 SAME-DAY pairing of a $500M buyback re-authorization with a $70-90M restructuring announcement (later doubled to $160M) is itself a tell. Then test: do insiders sell into the buyback prints? Form 4 + Item 5(c) buyback table cross-check.
rfm_tuples.M_value: CLO Mehri Shadman 11/15-11/18/2024: sold 26,879 Class C shares at $8.76-$8.81 = ~$236K. UAA executed ASR Dec 2024 at $8.76 average — the EXACT same price the insider sold at 30 days earlier. So the company was a buyer at $8.76 in Dec while the CLO was a seller at $8.76 in Nov. May 2024: Board authorizes new $500M buyback on SAME DAY (May 15 2024) it announces a restructuring plan and SAME DAY it later turns out (per Q1 10-Q) the securities-class-action settlement-discussion process was active (settlement reached 36 days later June 20 2024 for $434M). Cash $858.7M FY24; new $500M buyback authorized + $434M litigation accrual = $934M of capital commitments against $859M cash + ongoing operating losses (9M FY25 net loss $134M).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Three asymmetric capital-allocation tells stacked: (1) $500M buyback authorized the SAME DAY as a major restructuring announcement and ~5 weeks before agreeing to a $434M class-action settlement that would consume half of cash — this is buyback authorization as offset to bad news, not as conviction. (2) CLO sells 26,879 shares at $8.76 in mid-November; company executes ASR at $8.76 in mid-December — the insider sold to the company's buyback bid. (3) Total committed-capital ($500M buyback authority + $434M settlement = $934M) exceeds available cash ($859M) before the operating loss in FY25, meaning the buyback is being funded via DTC-channel margin and inventory reduction rather than free cash flow. The cleanest deterministic signal in this filing.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Executive Officers: 'Kevin Plank has been President and Chief Executive Officer since April 2024. He served as Executive Chair and Brand Chief from January 2020 through March 2024. Prior to that, he served as Chief Executive Officer and Chair of the Board of Directors from 1996, when he founded our Company, to 2019.' Exhibit 10.36: 'Separation Agreement between the Company and Stephanie C. Linnartz dated March 10, 2024, including General Release.' (Linnartz had been CEO from Feb 2023 to March 2024, ~13 months.) Exhibit 10.40: 'Separation Agreement between the Company and David Baxter dated January 29, 2024' (President Asia-Pacific). 10-K signed by Plank as CEO and David Bergman as CFO (Bergman in role since Nov 2017).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: insider-stability vs leadership-instability tell. Three CEOs in three years (Frisk → Linnartz Feb 2023 → Plank April 2024) is a top-tier instability signal. The founder displacing his hand-picked CEO 13 months after appointment with no permanent search means there is no succession bench. Bergman CFO tenure is stable (positive), but the CEO churn pattern dominates.
rfm_tuples.M_value: CEO sequence: Patrik Frisk (2020-Feb 2023, 30 months), Stephanie Linnartz (Feb 2023-March 2024, 13 months), Kevin Plank (April 2024-present). Linnartz separation Mar 10 2024 → Plank takes CEO role Apr 2024. Baxter (President Asia-Pacific) separation Jan 29 2024. Colin Browne employment agreement June 26 2023 (per Exhibit 10.39) — Browne was COO. Yassine Saidi as Chief Product Officer is new. Jim Dausch promoted to Chief Strategy & Consumer Experience Officer May 2024 (joined July 2023). Shawn Curran Chief Supply Chain Officer since Oct 2023. So in addition to CEO turnover, the entire C-suite was reshuffled in 2023-2024 with only Bergman (CFO) and Plank (now back) as continuity.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Two CEO transitions in 14 months is a leadership-stability red flag — Linnartz was hand-picked by Plank as Executive Chair, given a 13-month runway, and then displaced by Plank himself who never relinquished controlling stock (Class B convertible held by Plank). This is NOT a clean Mode-B 'lying' signal but it is a strong governance-instability tell that compounds with: (a) the class-action settlement requiring separated Chair/CEO roles (so Plank cannot reclaim Chair while CEO), (b) the material weakness, (c) the doubled restructuring. The athletic-apparel competitive set (Nike, adidas, lululemon, Hoka/Deckers, On) all have stable senior leadership; UAA's churn is anomalous. CFO continuity is the one positive — Bergman has signed every 10-K and 10-Q including the period of alleged 'pull-forward' sales (2015-2019), which the cynical reading interprets as 'the same CFO is signing the revisions to the financials he originally signed.'

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K MD&A: 'No single customer accounted for more than 10% of the Company's net revenues for Fiscal 2024.' Note 12: 'For Fiscal 2024, Fiscal 2023 and the Transition Period, no single customer accounted for more than 10% of the Company's net revenues. For Fiscal 2021, one customer within the North America region accounted for approximately 11% of the Company's net revenues.' Wholesale channel = 57% of FY24 net revenues; North America = 61% of net revenues ($3.2B in U.S.). 'In Fiscal 2024, sales through our wholesale channel represented approximately 57% of our net revenues.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: customer concentration disclosure-evasion tell. UAA distributes through Dick's Sporting Goods / Academy / Kohl's / DSW / off-price (Ross, TJX). Just under 10% is the SEC threshold for naming a customer; disclosing 'no customer > 10%' while sitting at, say, 9.5% at Dick's + 9.5% at Kohl's would still represent ~20% concentration with two wholesalers. Test against industry: athletic apparel wholesale is heavily consolidated. Mode-B: assess whether disclosure is structured around the 10% threshold to avoid naming customers.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY24 disclosure is binary: 'no single customer > 10%.' FY21 the company DID cross 10% for one NA customer (approximately 11%). The fact that the threshold-crossing happened in FY21 and FY24 is 'no customer > 10%' is consistent with either (a) genuine de-concentration, or (b) deliberate channel-management to stay just under threshold. The 10-K does not disclose: top-3 wholesale customer % of revenue, top-5 % of revenue, off-price channel % of revenue. Competitive context: Dick's Sporting Goods 2024 10-K identifies Nike at ~17% and adidas at ~5% of vendor purchases; the inverse view of Dick's-as-customer for UAA implies UAA is materially exposed to Dick's order patterns even if technically <10% of revenue.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Single-line 'no customer > 10%' disclosure is technically compliant but represents minimum-disclosure framing for a 57%-wholesale, North-America-concentrated apparel business. The 10-K could (but does not) disclose the top-3 wholesale customers in aggregate (which would be material and which counterparties — e.g., Dick's 2024 vendor mix — would corroborate via inverse mirror). The FY21→FY24 trajectory from 11% to <10% probably reflects (a) shifts within wholesale composition and (b) DTC channel growing as a denominator, but the disclosure is structured to communicate the minimum. Not a primary signal but a consistent pattern with the material-weakness / litigation / restructuring posture: minimum-disclosure orientation.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K balance sheet & MD&A: cash and equivalents $858.7M at 3/31/2024 ($632.2M / ~74% held by foreign subsidiaries 'indefinitely reinvested'). Q3 FY25 10-Q (Dec 31 2024) income statement: 9M FY25 net revenues $3,983.7M vs $4,369.7M prior year (-8.8%); 9M FY25 net loss $(133.8)M vs +$225.5M prior year; 9M FY25 loss from operations $(113.1)M vs +$233.3M prior year. Q3 alone: revenue -5.7%; wholesale -1.0%; DTC -9.1%; apparel -5.0%, footwear -9.0%; NA -7.8%, APAC -5.1%, LatAm -15.5%. 1.50% Convertible Senior Notes ($80.9M) matured June 1, 2024 and were repaid in cash.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: forward liquidity / capital-call coverage. Cash $859M minus (a) $434M settlement obligation + (b) $500M new buyback authority + (c) $80.9M convert maturity June 2024 + (d) $140-160M restructuring cash charges + (e) 9M FY25 operating losses $113M. Test whether the company can fund all five.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Cash uses post 3/31/24: convert repayment $80.9M (done June 2024); settlement $434M (Q3 10-Q discloses fully accrued); restructuring $50M cash component initially → $75M (per Sept 5 expansion); buyback $24.4M executed Q3 + $435M remaining authorized; operating loss 9M FY25 ($113M). Approximate cash drawdown FY25 if all executed: $80.9M + $434M + $75M + $24.4M + ($113M operating loss × 4/3 annualization=$150M) ≈ $764M against $859M starting cash before any working-capital benefit. Q3 FY25 inventory has been worked down (FY24 cash flow shows $216M inventory release), partially offsetting. NO going-concern language; '$858.7 million of cash and cash equivalents ... believe ... adequate to meet our liquidity needs and capital expenditure requirements for at least the next twelve months.'
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Liquidity is not yet a crisis but the runway is much tighter than the May 2024 10-K narrative suggests. Adding up known commitments ($434M settlement + $75M cash restructuring + $80.9M convert + $24M Q3 buyback already done + 9M operating loss) consumes ~$720M of ~$859M cash before any further FY26 buyback or restructuring. The remaining $435M buyback authority through May 2027 is essentially uncoverable from current cash if the settlement is paid in full upfront. Management's 12-month liquidity reaffirmation is technically correct but is dependent on continued inventory release and working-capital optimization, not on operating cash flow — a fragile position for a brand-rebuild story. The $632M held foreign-indefinitely-reinvested is the buffer; repatriation has tax cost (FX + foreign withholding), so the practical liquidity is closer to $227M domestic.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K MD&A 'Operating loss in our Corporate Other non-operating segment increased by $95.4 million to $782.4 million from $687.0 million. This was primarily due to higher litigation reserve, net losses arising from foreign currency hedges, and higher incentive compensation expenses, partially offset by lower consulting expenses.' Statements of Operations: Restructuring and impairment charges $56.7M FY24 vs $0 FY23. SG&A $2,400.5M FY24 vs $2,380.2M FY23. Net revenues $5,701.9M FY24 vs $5,903.2M FY23 (-3.4%). Gross profit FY24 $2,630.3M (margin 46.1%) vs $2,643.8M FY23 (44.8%) — gross margin +130 bps.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: 'higher litigation reserve' is buried inside Corporate Other segment commentary without quantification. The $95.4M YoY increase in Corp Other operating loss is partly the litigation reserve increase, but the 10-K does NOT disclose the litigation reserve amount. Test against the subsequent disclosure (Q1 FY25 10-Q with $434M settlement) — was the litigation reserve in FY24 anywhere close to $434M, or was the bulk of the settlement accrued post-10K?
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K (May 29 2024) discloses 'higher litigation reserve' qualitatively but does not state amount. Class-action settlement reached 22 days later (June 20 2024) for $434M. Subsequent-event disclosure in 10-K (Note 22) does NOT include the settlement amount — even though by the time of filing (May 29 2024) the settlement negotiations were almost certainly advanced (formal agreement 22 days later). The Q1 FY25 10-Q (Aug 8 2024) confirms settlement reached but does not retrospectively quantify the FY24 litigation reserve component. The pre-Settlement litigation reserve appears to have been materially below $434M.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: A $434M settlement reached 22 days after the 10-K filing means the settlement was substantially negotiated DURING the 10-K drafting period — yet no specific reserve quantum was disclosed, no specific subsequent-event language was added, and the litigation posture remained 'will defend vigorously.' This is the cleanest Mode-B catch in the file: the 10-K reader on May 29 2024 cannot derive the $434M figure but a 10-Q reader 70 days later sees it. A more honest 10-K would have either (a) disclosed an accrued contingency reserve at or near the eventual settlement amount, or (b) explicitly flagged active settlement negotiations as a subsequent event. The choice not to do either is information-asymmetry by design and is precisely the kind of disclosure-evasion that the class action ITSELF alleged in the underlying claims.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K: 'We have served as the Company's auditor since 2003.' /s/ PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, Baltimore, Maryland, May 29, 2024. Critical Audit Matter = REVENUE RECOGNITION ('the principal consideration for our determination that performing procedures relating to revenue recognition is a critical audit matter is a high degree of auditor effort in performing procedures relating to the Company's revenue recognition'). 10-K Item 9: 'CHANGES IN AND DISAGREEMENTS WITH ACCOUNTANTS ON ACCOUNTING AND FINANCIAL DISCLOSURE — None.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: auditor history check. Mode B: assess intersection of (a) PwC selecting revenue recognition as its sole Critical Audit Matter, (b) the class action alleging improper 'pull forward' sales / sales-period shifting, (c) the FY24 material weakness in period-end reporting requiring prior-period revenue revision. All three independent vectors converge on REVENUE.
rfm_tuples.M_value: PwC: continuous auditor since 2003 (21 years), no resignation, no disagreement disclosed, unqualified opinion FY24. Sole CAM = revenue recognition. Concurrent vectors on revenue: (1) Plaintiff allegations 2015-2019 of sales-period shifting ('pull forward'); (2) FY24 prior-period revision corrected overstated revenues (promotional gift card / e-commerce errors); (3) Material weakness in 'period-end financial reporting process' implicating revenue cutoff and reconciliations; (4) PwC CAM specifically calls out testing 'completeness, accuracy, and occurrence of revenue ... obtaining and inspecting source documents, such as purchase orders, invoices, proof of shipment, and subsequent cash receipts' — i.e., the same procedures that would be relevant to a 'pull forward' allegation.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Auditor governance is technically clean — no resignation, no disagreement, no qualification. But the Mode-B convergence is striking: PwC's CAM, the class-action allegations, the prior-period revisions, and the material weakness ALL converge on revenue recognition controls. A long-tenured auditor (21 years) signing off on the company's revenue controls while simultaneously selecting revenue as its sole CAM and while management itself admits to revenue-side errors requiring revision is the kind of finding that elevates auditor INDEPENDENCE-IN-FACT questions. Within the honesty-alpha framework, this is honest reporting by both management and auditor — but the picture they jointly paint is of a company where revenue is the single most-scrutinized line item and has been for years.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K MD&A: 'On May 15, 2024, subsequent to the fiscal year end, our Board of Directors authorized the repurchase of up to $500 million ... of outstanding shares of our Class C Common Stock through May 31, 2027.' Combined with Fiscal 2025 Restructuring Plan ($70-90M, later $140-160M), $434M securities class action settlement (Q1 FY25), continued material weakness through Q3 FY25, three CEO transitions in 36 months, founder controls Class B convertible stock. Sponsorships and other contractual commitments $431.7M total. Top-5 fabric suppliers = 38% of fabric in apparel and accessories (concentration in Taiwan / Jordan / Vietnam / Malaysia / China).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: counterparty mirror + sector-specific tell. Athletic apparel competitive context: Nike, adidas, lululemon, Hoka/Deckers, On Holding. UAA brand-positioning narrative ('premium brand-right growth', 'reduce discounting and promotional activity') is a wholesale-de-emphasis story in a category where DTC and brand cool are the value drivers. Test: is the brand-rebuild narrative supported by revenue trajectory?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 FY25 10-Q (Aug 2024) 'we continued to face a challenging retail environment, particularly in North America, that included lower demand in our wholesale channel, in addition to the impacts of proactive strategies to reduce discounting and promotional activity in our direct-to-consumer channel, particularly in e-commerce ... Total net revenues decreased 10.1%. Within our channels, wholesale revenue decreased 8.3%.' Q3 FY25 (Dec 2024 quarter): revenue -5.7%, DTC -9.1%, NA -7.8%, footwear -9.0%. Brand-rebuild narrative is being executed via wholesale shrinkage + DTC margin defense, but the absolute revenue trajectory is consistently negative across all three pre-cutoff 10-Qs and accelerated post-10K. 9M FY25 revenue -8.8% YoY. Sponsorship commitment $432M = significant fixed cost in a declining-revenue base.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The brand-rebuild story is real but the timing is brutal — Plank has returned to a brand that is being repositioned upmarket while consumer-discretionary athleisure is being captured by Hoka, On, lululemon, and Nike's value-tier. The DTC -9.1% / footwear -9.0% Q3 numbers are particularly damaging because DTC margin and footwear penetration are the two metrics that competitors use to underwrite premium pricing. Sponsorship commitments ($432M, of which $152M due in less than one year) are a fixed-cost liability against shrinking revenue. This is a legitimate brand-turnaround story (Mode A: management is honest about the challenges), but Mode B says: the narrative requires DTC and footwear to grow, and they are shrinking faster than wholesale. The honesty-alpha framework treats this as MODERATE because management's disclosure is candid (revenue decline, restructuring honesty) — the SHORT case is built more on the cluster of governance + ICFR + litigation + asymmetric capital allocation tells (C1, C2, C3, C4, C8) than on this sector signal alone.

supplemental_signals.founder_control_class_b: Plank holds the Class B Convertible Common Stock (34.45M shares) plus is now CEO again — re-concentration of power in a company forced by class-action settlement to formally separate Chair/CEO roles for 3 years (the settlement only restricts the CEO-Chair combination, not Plank's voting control via Class B).
supplemental_signals.fiscal_year_change: Changed fiscal year end from Dec 31 to Mar 31 effective FY2023 (3-month Transition Period Jan-Mar 2022). FY-year changes are themselves a moderate signal but here it was disclosed cleanly.
supplemental_signals.five_year_stock_chart: 10-K stock performance graph: $100 invested 12/31/2018 = $41.75 on 3/31/2024 (-58.3%); S&P 500 in same period $229.08 (+129%); S&P 500 Apparel index $57.12 (-42.9%). UAA underperformed both broad market and apparel peers by wide margin over five years.
supplemental_signals.deferred_tax_valuation_allowance: DTA valuation allowance grew from $177.0M FY23 to $274.8M FY24 (+$97.8M charge), implying management does not expect to realize ~$98M of NOLs / DTAs in U.S. taxable income — quiet acknowledgment of impaired earnings outlook.
supplemental_signals.no_dividend: No cash dividend in Fiscal 2024, 2023, 2021 or Transition Period; 'we do not anticipate paying any cash dividends in the foreseeable future' + credit-facility may limit dividend ability.
supplemental_signals.form_4_insider_sell_into_buyback: CLO Mehri Shadman Form 4 11/19/2024: sold 26,879 Class C shares at $8.76-$8.81 on 11/15-11/18; company ASR Dec 2024 at $8.76 average. Insider-vs-calendar match.
supplemental_signals.credit_agreement_amendment_4: Amendment No. 4 to credit agreement dated March 6, 2024 — fourth amendment to facility (Amendments 1-3 in May 2020 / May 2021 / Dec 2021 covered COVID period). Amendment 4 timing pre-restructuring announcement.
supplemental_signals.convertible_repayment_june_2024: $80.9M 1.50% Convertible Senior Notes matured 6/1/2024 and were repaid in cash from balance sheet (per 10-K plan, confirmed in pre-cutoff 10-Qs).

summary: UAA is a control-survivor name where the FY24 10-K + three pre-cutoff 10-Qs paint a cluster of textbook forensic tells: (1) unremediated material weakness in period-end financial reporting requiring prior-period revenue/COGS/SG&A revision; (2) restructuring plan that DOUBLED from $70-90M to $140-160M within 110 days of announcement; (3) securities class action settled for $434M just 22 days after 10-K filing with no quantification in the 10-K subsequent-events note; (4) $500M buyback authorized on the SAME DAY as the restructuring announcement and 35 days before the $434M settlement was reached, with CLO selling at $8.76 immediately before the company bought back at $8.76; (5) founder-CEO whiplash with three CEOs in 36 months; (6) PwC's sole Critical Audit Matter (revenue recognition) converges with the alleged 'pull forward' practices, the material weakness, and the prior-period revisions. Honesty-alpha framework: management's disclosures are mostly literally true but exhibit consistent minimum-disclosure framing and the divergence between the 10-K litigation posture ('will defend vigorously') and the 22-days-later $434M settlement is the kind of asymmetry the framework was built to flag. SHORT-tier verdict justified.
